subject: Redwood Dedicated: pool capacity governance & onboarding checklist

Subject: Redwood Dedicated — initial capacity/governance questions

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re excited to move forward with Redwood Dedicated for inference on our customer-facing image-understanding service. Before we lock the SOW, the infra team asked for clarity on a few things so our procurement and NetOps can finalize region choices and the autoscale budget. High level asks: 

- Minimum guaranteed throughput (GPU hours / vGPU baseline) vs burst headroom: how granular are the guarantees by pool?
- Warm pool policy: time-to-warm for cached KV for cold-starts and any recommended pre-warm thresholds.
- Regional placement: we want a primary in us-west and a hot-failover in us-east; what limits the second region selection (data residency, capacity availability, costs)?
- Ops handoff doc: can you share a single checklist the CS/infra teams can follow for provisioning and acceptance?

We can share an internal diagram of request patterns if that helps. Would love to get answers before Friday so we can keep the SOW signature on schedule.

Best,
Jordan
Head of SRE, Helios AI

From: rachel_kim@redwood.com
To: Jordan Park <jordan@helios.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood Dedicated — initial capacity/governance questions

Jordan — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together answers and a short onboarding checklist (attached) for the CS -> NetOps handoff. Quick summary below; attachments have the detail we typically run during activation.

1) Guarantees vs burst headroom:
   - We define a guaranteed baseline as the reserved GPU capacity in the pool (committed GPUs). That maps to predictable slots per second depending on model selection and instance size.
   - Burst headroom is provided by our autoscale policy and optional multipool bursting; typical safe burst is 1.5x–2x the baseline for short windows (minutes) depending on regional spare capacity.

2) Warm pool policy / cold-starts:
   - KV cache warmup: recommend a 30–45 minute pre-warm window for large-context models; smaller models typically stabilize in 10–15 minutes.
   - We can pre-warm by synthetic traffic or by seeding common prefixes (we include a pre-warm script in the checklist).

3) Regional placement constraints:
   - Primary us-west for latency works. Hot-failover in us-east supported; limits are capacity availability and cross-region data transfer policy (we keep KV caches local unless you opt-in to cross-region replication).
   - If Helios needs guaranteed failover SLOs, we recommend reserved baseline in both regions (cost tradeoff) or an agreed fallback policy with max warmup time.

4) Ops handoff doc: attached XLSX with sequential acceptance steps (network, IAM, test prompts, KV warm, traffic ramp).

Ben / Soojin — can you weigh in on acceptable default autoscale breakpoints and whether we should propose 1.75x burst cap for Helios?

Rachel
Senior CS Manager | Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: rachel_kim@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: Jordan Park <jordan@helios.ai>
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 11:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood Dedicated — initial capacity/governance questions

Looping in pricing context for the burst recommendations. Short answer: 1.75x is a reasonable default for negotiated deals — it limits exposure while offering meaningful headroom. A few notes: 

- Billing model: baseline is billed at committed reserved rate; burst usage is billed at a higher on-demand multiplier. We can cap daily burst spend and alert Helios if spend approaches threshold.
- Autoscale breakpoints: recommend two tiers: conservative (1.25x sustained, 1.75x short burst) and aggressive (2.0x short burst) for launch windows. For Helios, given real-time SLAs, start conservative and open to a short launch window at 2.0x.
- Reporting: we'll enable per-route token-level cost and hourly burst usage in Console for transparency.

Soojin — can you confirm ops readiness and whether the pre-warm script aligns with our staging playbook? If so, I’ll put the 1.75x default into the SOW as the negotiated burst cap and add a clause for a 72-hour launch evaluation window.

Ben
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: rachel_kim@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: Jordan Park <jordan@helios.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood Dedicated — initial capacity/governance questions

We validated the pre-warm script against our staging templates — it warms KV and populates caches in the expected timeframes. A couple of implementation notes for NetOps: 

- Network & IAM: please ensure the customer VPC peering is approved and routes to the dedicated control plane subnets; we'll need a security group allowing control-plane TLS and a few ephemeral ports for agent heartbeats.
- Observability gates: enable tracing hooks and per-request sampling at 5% during warmup, ramp to 25% during evaluation window. That helps validate cold-start distribution.
- Failover choreography: our recommended flow is active-passive with traffic-shift in three 10-minute increments; document includes CLI commands for rollback.

Jordan — if NetOps can confirm peering/route acceptance by Monday, we can schedule a staged pre-warm on Tuesday (non-production) and a production ramp on Thursday. I've attached the updated autoscale PDF with CLI snippets.

Soojin
